question: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched? [Sir Thomas Roe — Arrival and destination of the English embassy]
options: Surat — The port where Sir Thomas Roe landed in September 1615 as the accredited ambassador of King James I
Ajmer — The temporary Mughal court where Sir Thomas Roe presented his credentials to Emperor Jahangir and resided for nearly three years
Agra — The main Mughal capital city where the English secured permission to establish a factory under Roe's farman
Goa — The Portuguese capital where Sir Thomas Roe successfully negotiated a joint Anglo-Portuguese naval treaty in 1616
wrong_fact: Sir Thomas Roe did NOT negotiate a treaty in Goa, nor was he sent to the Portuguese. Goa was the stronghold of the Portuguese Estado da India, who were the main rivals of the English. Roe's mission was directed to the Mughal Emperor Jahangir to secure trading rights for the British East India Company and to counter Portuguese influence at the Mughal court.
explanation: Sir Thomas Roe was sent by King James I of England as a royal ambassador to the Mughal court. He arrived at Surat in 1615 and traveled to Ajmer, where Emperor Jahangir was holding court. Roe spent his time there negotiating for trade privileges, which resulted in imperial orders allowing the English to establish factories at Agra, Ahmedabad, and Broach. He did not visit Goa, which was controlled by the hostile Portuguese.

question: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched? [Sir Thomas Roe — Locations of English factories and court travels]
options: Ahmedabad — One of the key commercial centers in Gujarat where Roe successfully established an English factory
Broach (Bharuch) — An important port on the Narmada river where Roe obtained trading rights and a factory for cotton goods
Mandu — A historic fortress town in Madhya Pradesh where Roe accompanied Jahangir's royal camp in 1617 during the Deccan campaigns
Madras (Fort St. George) — The southern port where Roe personally purchased land in 1618 to construct the first English fort in South India
wrong_fact: Sir Thomas Roe did NOT purchase Madras or build Fort St. George. Madras was acquired much later, in 1639, by Francis Day from the local Nayak of Vandavasi, and Fort St. George was founded in 1640. Roe's embassy was active in Western and Northern India (Surat, Ajmer, Mandu, Ahmedabad, Agra) and did not involve the Coromandel coast.
explanation: During his embassy (1615-1619), Sir Thomas Roe traveled with Jahangir's court to Mandu and Ahmedabad. Under the imperial farmans he secured, the English East India Company established factories in Gujarat (Surat, Ahmedabad, Broach) and Uttar Pradesh (Agra). He had no connection with the acquisition of Madras (Fort St. George), which occurred decades later.

question: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched? [Sir Thomas Roe — Diplomatic strategy and regional negotiations]
options: Prince Khurram (Shah Jahan) — The Mughal prince and governor of Gujarat whom Roe had to negotiate with to secure the Surat trade privileges
Surat Factory — Roe advised the EIC against fortifying this factory, famously arguing that trade should be sought through peaceful commerce, not military force
Red Sea Trade — Roe actively organized English trade expeditions to Mocha (Yemen) to build trade links outside the Mughal domain
Masulipatnam — Roe traveled here in 1616 to negotiate the 'Golden Farman' directly with the Sultan of Golconda to secure the cloth trade
wrong_fact: Sir Thomas Roe did NOT travel to Masulipatnam, nor did he negotiate the Golden Farman. The Golden Farman was granted by the Sultan of Golconda to the English East India Company in 1632, long after Roe had returned to England. Roe's diplomatic mission was confined entirely to the Mughal territories under Jahangir.
explanation: Sir Thomas Roe had to negotiate extensively with Prince Khurram (the future Shah Jahan), who was governor of Gujarat and initially hostile to the English. Roe's policy for the Company was 'quiet trade' without the expense of military fortifications (unlike the Portuguese and Dutch). He also encouraged trade in the Red Sea (Mocha). Masulipatnam's Golden Farman (1632) was obtained by other English merchants and agents, not Sir Thomas Roe.
